questions.question_text: What is stage fright, as described in the chapter?

options.text: A rare condition that only affects professional speakers
A normal reaction involving physical and mental nervousness when speaking in front of others
A permanent fear that cannot be overcome with practice
A sign that someone is not meant to be a public speakerCorrect Answer:B. A normal reaction involving physical and mental nervousness when speaking in front of others

questions.question_text: According to the chapter, what is one benefit of using positive self-talk as a mindset shift for confidence?

options.text: It eliminates all physical symptoms of nervousness instantly
It helps replace negative thoughts with encouraging ones to reduce stress
It guarantees a perfect speech every time
It prevents the need for any practice before speakingCorrect Answer:B. It helps replace negative thoughts with encouraging ones to reduce stress

questions.question_text: How does the chapter suggest posture can impact a speaker’s confidence?

options.text: Slouching makes a speaker appear more relatable to the audience
Standing tall with shoulders back projects control and can make a speaker feel stronger
Posture has no effect on how a speaker is perceived by others
Only professional speakers need to worry about postureCorrect Answer:B. Standing tall with shoulders back projects control and can make a speaker feel stronger

questions.question_text: What is one purpose of recording oneself as a practice strategy, according to the chapter?

options.text: To share videos on social media for popularity
To spot habits like saying “um” or looking down and track improvement over time
To avoid practicing in front of others completely
To memorize speeches without needing to understand themCorrect Answer:B. To spot habits like saying “um” or looking down and track improvement over time

questions.question_text: Why does the chapter emphasize the importance of eye contact in body language?

options.text: It distracts the audience from noticing mistakes in the speech
It shows engagement and builds trust with listeners
It is only necessary for large audiences, not small groups
It makes the speaker appear less nervous without any effortCorrect Answer:B. It shows engagement and builds trust with listeners

questions.question_text: What is the main goal of reframing failure as growth, as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: To ignore mistakes and pretend they didn’t happen
To view mistakes as lessons that help improve future performances
To blame others for any errors during a speech
To avoid taking risks in public speaking altogetherCorrect Answer:B. To view mistakes as lessons that help improve future performances
